crop_note: scan cropped at or just inside the sheet edge; corners slightly worn/darkened
evidence: Title 'Departure of a Daimyō' and procession setting out past the teahouses plus a pink low horizon drive dawn; light streaky clouds over a pale sky. No plants or clothing cues for season.
taxonomy_friction: Season left null: no seasonal cue at all, and a flat 4-season vector would over-reward it; the schema needs an explicit 'season unknown' convention. Procession (daimyō departure) is the main subject but setting still dominates.

crop_note: sheet fills the frame with its cream margin; printed border line ~7% in
evidence: Title 'Snow on the Kiso Gorge'; white dots falling and snow-laden cliffs and pines. The dark navy sky slot could be snowstorm gloom or evening; time of day is a guess.
taxonomy_friction: Falling snow plus heavy lying snow has to be split 50/50 between snowfall and snow_cover, though both are fully present; snow_cover is defined as 'no snow falling', which makes them mutually exclusive in the definition but not in the vector. 'forest' flag is a stretch for scattered pines on cliffs; a 'gorge/cliff' feature is not expressible.

crop_note: scan cropped at the image border; no margin visible
evidence: Clear pale sky with a red horizon band under dark top bokashi; a skein of geese flying suggests autumn and possibly evening, but the red band may be convention, so time is partly a guess. Series places it in the autumn section.
taxonomy_friction: Marker list has 'wild geese (descending)' but here geese are flying in formation, not descending; I used wild_geese anyway. Marker names have no canonical IDs in TAXONOMY.md, so I invented snake_case ids (wild_geese, snow, new_year, summer_fireworks). Sumida river mouth into Edo Bay is between river and sea.

crop_note: sheet fills the frame; vertical join/fold line at centre (two-panel scan or paper join)
evidence: Blue sky with large billowing cloud and smoke from a fire; even daylight. Snow-capped Fuji is perennial and the sawyers' clothing gives no clear season.
taxonomy_friction: Labour scene (sawyers on a huge timber) dominates the composition; genre is borderline between figures_in_landscape and other. Place is only a province ('Tōtōmi sanchū'), so precision_km is very coarse; unclear whether province-level places should get coordinates at all. Big cumulus clouds in a blue sky: clear vs. cloudy split is arbitrary.

crop_note: full sheet with cream margin; title cartouche protrudes at right; worn edges
evidence: Clear peach-to-blue sky; kadomatsu-like pine/bamboo by the gate and a Sumiyoshi dance troupe with large umbrella point to New Year. Faint dawn feel from the warm sky (first-day-of-year?) is a guess; Edo Bay visible in the distance.
taxonomy_friction: New Year is lunar (late Jan–Feb in Edo) but the marker peaks 1 Jan, and the season vector forces winter vs spring (Edo New Year = start of spring). Odd small open circles float in the sky (not snow, maybe a kite/toy); nowhere to note unexplained motifs. Distant sea view vs. sea at the location are indistinguishable in the water vector.

crop_note: full sheet with margin on light backdrop; thin dark strip at far left edge
evidence: Clear pale sky with top bokashi (convention only), even light; green grass and pines suggest the warm half of the year but there is no specific seasonal plant, so season is weak.
taxonomy_friction: Season inferred only from 'green grass', which the conventions warn against (colour rather than plants); a 'low confidence' season vector and a null season behave very differently in matching.

place.name: Nagasaki harbour, view of Mt Inasa

crop_note: scan cropped at the sheet edge; no margin
evidence: Grey-toned mountains with stylised cloud bands and a red horizon band over a busy harbour; choppy waves and a full sail suggest breeze. Red band is probably convention, so dawn/dusk split is a hedge.
taxonomy_friction: Sky is mostly stylised bands and grey mountain tones, hard to say whether 'cloudy' is meant. No seasonal cue (season null). Mountains seen across the harbour: terrain at the viewpoint (on the water) is flat, but the scene reads as mountainous; the viewpoint-vs-scene rule from §7 isn't stated for environment.

crop_note: page fills the frame; fragments of another image visible at the left edge, suggesting a page from a book or album
evidence: Ink-and-grey close-up of a large-eyed bird (looks more like an owl or white bird than a sparrow) on bamboo with a small sparrow flying below; plain paper ground, no sky or setting.
taxonomy_friction: Possibly a book/album page (marks at left edge, monochrome sumi-and-grey, calligraphic title) which would require exclusion, but not certain, so included. Bamboo is evergreen and gives no season; every scoring dimension is null, so the print can only ever score neutral and would surface at random.

crop_note: sheet fills the frame; printed border with notched corners
evidence: Still life of a mackerel and a halibut with leaves and grass spikes on a plain ground. Season only from the haiku convention of autumn mackerel (aki-saba); low confidence.
taxonomy_friction: Fish still life is not bird-and-flower and not a scene; the genre list has no 'still life / fish' category. Seasonal association of food (aki-saba) has no marker; I did not invent one. Environment null although the subject is marine.

crop_note: small card fills the frame; printed English caption strip along the bottom (~bottom 7%) and Japanese publisher text at lower right; image area inside a printed frame
evidence: Later postcard-sized reproduction of Hiroshige's Hōeidō Hiratsuka: courier running along a winding causeway, Kōma-yama with snowy Fuji behind; pale grey-blue haze around the hills, pinkish top bokashi. No season cues.
taxonomy_friction: This is a Meiji-or-later reproduction card (English caption 'No.8 Hiratsuka...'), not an original print; the brief has no rule for reproductions/postcards or for printed captions that should be cropped out. Flooded paddies vs. water category is ambiguous.

exclude_reason: Warrior/legend print (Ushiwakamaru from a Yoshitsune biography series); figure dominates
crop_note: sheet on light backdrop with an X-Rite colour bar/ruler at right (x > ~0.93); trim sheet edges, colour bar must be excluded
evidence: Crescent moon, dark grey sky and metadata 'bij nacht' give night; faint vertical streaks in the sky may be rain/mist or just woodgrain, so weather is uncertain. Torii and stone lantern up steps, cryptomeria forest, waterfall.
taxonomy_friction: Faint vertical lines in a night sky: rain vs. woodgrain vs. mist is undecidable at 800 px. A waterfall's plunge stream is coded 'river' because water has no waterfall/mountain-stream category (only a flag). Place inferred from the inscription naming Kurama/Kibune, not the title.

exclude_reason: Uchiwa-e (fan print) of a comic fox-dance figure assembled from objects; no landscape scene
crop_note: full uchiwa-e sheet; fan-shaped printed area with uncut handle notch at bottom centre (white semicircle is the notch, not a moon)
evidence: Fox figure built from a pot, dishes, pipe and cloth dancing around a trap of spinning tops; fans imitating stacked rice sheaves (per metadata) hint at harvest/autumn. Dark top and blue lower ground are decorative.
taxonomy_friction: Fan prints have a non-rectangular image area; crop as [x,y,w,h] cannot express it. The white semicircle at the bottom could be mis-read as a rising moon.

crop_note: full sheet with cream margin on light backdrop
evidence: Dark night sky with a rocket trail and a starburst, lantern-lit pleasure boats under the bridge; Ryōgoku fireworks opened the summer river-cooling season. Smoky glow around the burst read as slight haze.
taxonomy_friction: Is a night sky without visible clouds 'clear'? Fireworks smoke is not weather mist. The white burst could be mis-read as a moon by a careless tagger.

exclude_reason: Surimono calendar print (egoyomi, 1805) with poems; figures (Ōhara women and oxen) dominate, setting minimal
crop_note: sheet nearly fills frame on light backdrop; soft muted surimono colours
evidence: Procession of Ōhara women carrying firewood with laden oxen on a green slope; no sky. Season guessed only from it being a New Year calendar print (firewood gathering, winter-to-spring).
taxonomy_friction: New Year greeting/calendar prints are tied to the year's start in meaning but the scene itself shows no New Year marker; unclear whether to use new_year.

exclude_reason: Book cover (Hokusai, One Hundred Views of Mt Fuji, vol. 2); not a print scene
crop_note: closed book on light backdrop; yellow cover with title slip, stab binding at right
evidence: Image is the plain yellow cover of the Fugaku hyakkei volume 2 with title slip; no picture.
taxonomy_friction: fuji=false although the book is about Fuji (none visible). Whole-book records should probably be filtered before tagging.

crop_note: scan cropped at/near the sheet edge; notched-corner printed border
evidence: Pale yellow horizon glow under blue top bokashi, Fuji at left through a pine avenue across wet paddies; soft haze on distant trees. Yellow glow gives no clear dawn/dusk cue, so split; season only from green paddy grass.
taxonomy_friction: Flooded rice paddies / marshland have no water category (coded partly as 'lake'). A pine-lined causeway (namiki) is coded as 'forest', which overstates it; an 'avenue/namiki' feature would help.

crop_note: uchiwa-e: fan-shaped image on a rectangular sheet; sheet fills frame
evidence: Title 'Snow'; snowflakes against a dark grey sky, snow on roofs, lantern, komainu and street; figures under snow-laden umbrellas. Dark sky may be snow gloom or evening; time is a guess.
taxonomy_friction: Borderline include: two beauties under umbrellas are large in the foreground, but the snowy street and shrine precinct dominate. Uchiwa-e fan shape is not an 'extreme format' per the brief but is non-rectangular. 'Famous Places of Edo: Snow' names no locatable place, so place null.

exclude_reason: Figure print (mitate of Komachi praying for rain: courtesan and attendant); no setting
crop_note: sheet on light backdrop; handwritten inventory number in left margin; fibrous paper edges
evidence: Fine slanted rain lines across a plain grey ground, figure holding an umbrella; no setting or time cues.
taxonomy_friction: Strong weather signal but no setting at all; excluded per genre rule even though it is one of the clearest rain images in the batch.

crop_note: full sheet with cream margin fills the frame
evidence: Dense falling flakes against a grey-blue sky; snow thick on trees, bridge and banks; travellers with snow-covered hats. 'Yūhi-no-oka' (Sunset Hill) is a place name, not a time cue; time of day is a guess.
taxonomy_friction: Title contains 夕日 (evening sun) as part of a place name; the 'decide dawn/dusk from title kanji' rule would mislead here. snowfall vs snow_cover split again forced 50/50 when both are fully present.

crop_note: sheet with cream margin fills the frame; title cartouche slightly outside the border at upper right
evidence: Clear sky with red horizon band, geese flying in a V over the bay, travellers climbing the pine-covered slope. Red band plus flying birds tilt toward dusk, but no title cue, so time split; geese give autumn (or spring return).
taxonomy_friction: Flying geese can mean autumn arrival or spring departure; the marker is defined for 'descending' geese only. 'forest' flag is weak for a pine-clad headland.
